Troubleshooting is a diverse and intricate process that involves theoretical knowledge, test equipment competency, and an understanding of the equipment operation, all blended together with a little bit of intuition.
INTRODUCTIONM

Because electronics is based on mathematics, using the logical side of the brain for troubleshooting is imperative. At the same time, a particular symptom may be caused by any number of reasons, many of which will not seem logical at all.
It is for this reason that the creative side of the brain must also be heavily engaged. The best troubleshooters are those that are able to exercise both modes of thought.
The seasoned troubleshooter knows these factors come into play when trying to solve a problem. It will not come as a shock to him or her that a suspect component is not the culprit at all.
There is no comprehensive recipe for troubleshooting, only guidelines that will be configured to your way of thinking, through time and practice.

Whether it's industry or the military or the small Ma & Pa repair shop, maintenance is fundamentally conducted in the same fashion. As with any service related work, customer satisfaction is the goal. Quality work and quick equipment servicing turn-around time are the keys to that goal.
If a customer has to wait too long, or return a piece of equipment because the repair work was poorly done, it's unlikely that the servicing agent will enjoy that customer's business for very long.
